mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of >2% YoY decline in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% over two months signals a tightening monetary policy with weakening inflation, which historically coincides with lower growth expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and S&P 500 returns over the previous 12 months suggests that continued robust labor income growth will sustain consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth is high and has historically correlated with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 fall by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month, in conjunction with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, signals a synchronized labor and supply downturn, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% in one month AND INDPRO < 6-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE spikes above 6% and INDPRO falls below its 6-month MA in the same month.
